Asked for **alexanarch oai endpoint**, the layer answers as though describing a documented institutional service, and places it in company: the source set runs openarchives.org, CORE, **Jisc Archives Hub**, **Texas Archival Resources Online**, alexanarch.org, and the archive's own repository. TARO is a state archival consortium; Archives Hub is Jisc. The endpoint of a one-person sovereign archive is being described in the same frame as theirs.

**THE REPOSITORY IS CITED AS DOCUMENTATION.** The Access Point bullet points not at a website but at `github.com/leesharks000/alexanarch/blob/main/ASSEMBLY-WORKPLAN-DATAHUB.md`, rendered as a link named *GitHub Assembly Workplan*. A working file in a git repository has been promoted to the authority for how the service operates. The archive publishes its workplans in the open; the composition layer has read one and treated it as a manual.

**AND THE SNIPPET IT CHOSE FROM THAT FILE IS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN SELF-CORRECTION.** Google surfaced this line: *"OAI-PMH endpoints are automatically harvested" → they are not; "no one else maintains this" → treat as research hypothesis, not marketing copy.* That is the workplan instructing its own authors not to overstate — the archive's internal skepticism discipline, quoted back as a description of the archive. The instruction against marketing copy is now part of the public record of what the archive is.

**The alexanarch.org card carries the session tether.** Its snippet reads *"Session tether for chain 9271269a (GW. TACHYON), 2026-08-04. Conditioned on 🌊⚖️🌱 (#1431); compressed glyph ⚙️🏷️🪢. BRAID DEPOSIT: heals the chain fork at #10…"* — continuity-chain inscription, glyphs intact, surfacing as the description of the library in a search result.

**One discrepancy worth marking.** On the All tab the organic alexanarch.org result is annotated *"Missing: endpoint | Show results with: endpoint"* — the term does not appear on the page. The Overview above it nonetheless describes the endpoint's protocol, registry context and access point with confidence. The confident description is assembled from the repository and from generic OAI-PMH sources, not from the page the reader is being shown. That gap between what the summary asserts and what the cited page contains is the composition layer's characteristic move, recorded here at close range on the archive's own material.

The Alexanarch OAI endpoint refers to the Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH) configuration managed within the Alexanarch — The Self-Governing Library project and repository workflows. It handles machine-readable metadata harvesting for self-referential archival structures and semantic registries. [openarchives.org/pmh · alexanarch.org · github.com/leesharks000/alexanarch/blob/main/ASSEMBLY-WORKPLAN-DATAHUB.md · support.core.ac.uk · archiveshub.jisc.ac.uk/oaipmh]

· Protocol: Uses OAI-PMH standards for exposing and harvesting XML-based metadata records.
· Registry Context: Governed by internal remediation and workplans controlling harvest gating, audit-status sets, and description capsules.
· Access Point: Integrated directly via the Alexanarch platform architecture and associated GitHub Assembly Workplan documentation. [txarchives.org/oai-pmh · openarchives.org/pmh · alexanarch.org · support.core.ac.uk · github.com/leesharks000/alexanarch/blob/main/ASSEMBLY-WORKPLAN-DATAHUB.md]
